fixes.explanation: Bethsaida is the destination, baker. Mark says Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to Bethsaida, while He dismissed the crowd (Mark 6:45). The boat had a heading before it ever left the shore. That's more planning than I did for my last batch, and I had a recipe card.

That would be a problem, friend, but Mark doesn't say it. The reason he gives is that the wind was against them (Mark 6:48). He says nothing about a leak. I'd rather bail out a mixing bowl than a boat anyway.

A snapped oar would be rough, but it's not in the text, baker. Mark says they were straining to row because the wind was against them (Mark 6:48). The wind is the reason he gives, and he says nothing about an oar breaking.
That's it, baker. Jesus says, "Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid." (Mark 6:50). Mark says He spoke up at once. Hearing a voice you know right when you're scared is a gift.

That sounds like a coach, friend, but it's not what Jesus says. He tells them, "Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid." (Mark 6:50). Rowing harder isn't in His words. He tells them to take courage, and He tells them who He is.
False is right, friend. Mark says Jesus climbed into the boat with them, "…and the wind died down." (Mark 6:51). After all that straining, the wind dies down instead of picking up.

The loaves, baker. Mark says the disciples were utterly astounded, "…for they had not understood about the loaves…" (Mark 6:52). That points back to the feeding of the crowd just before this (Mark 6:41-44). Mark names the loaves as the thing they hadn't understood.
True, baker. Mark says that "As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognized Jesus" (Mark 6:54). There's no waiting around and no wondering who He was. They knew Him right away.

Bread and fish were part of the feeding of the crowd earlier in the chapter, friend (Mark 6:41-44). But here, Mark says they carried "…the sick on mats…" (Mark 6:55). The people came to Jesus carrying those who needed healing. Good memory, though.

The boat is in this story, friend, but it's not what they asked to touch. Mark says they begged Him "…just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak." (Mark 6:56). The edge of His cloak is the answer.
